notes: Four-lane parallel sweep (ai / bigtech+hardware+mobile / devtools+cloud / security) via background subagents, covering 2026-10-04 and 2026-10-05. All lanes hit routine EGRESS_BLOCKED on org-domain WebFetch (openai.com, blog.google, apple.com/newsroom, nvidianews.nvidia.com, news.samsung.com, endoflife.date, aws.amazon.com/new, azure.microsoft.com/updates, cisa.gov) and worked from WebSearch snippets instead; anthropic.com/news fetched directly in the AI lane with nothing new past what's already filed. Unusually thin day for genuinely new material: most lane findings turned out to be rediscoveries of items already on the calendar with better or equal sourcing (CES 2027, MWC Barcelona 2027, AWS re:Invent 2026, NeurIPS 2026, NSA CNSA 2.0 mandate, Oracle CPU Jan 2027, Let's Encrypt 64-day default profile, Google Play Contacts/Location policy, Google Play 16KB page-size deadline, Kubernetes 1.35 EOL) — left untouched since they added no new information. Only four new, well-sourced items survived: Marvell's Oct 6 Investor Day, a Washington State AI-companion-chatbot law taking effect Jan 2027, AKS's Kubernetes 1.34 extended-support end date, and SAP's November 2026 Security Patch Day. Declined to file: a Google Cloud Next 2027 date (6th consecutive run with only third-party-aggregator sourcing), an Azure OpenAI GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini Oct 1 retirement claim (conflicts with the existing Dec 9 entry and is sourced to a low-quality aggregator), a GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18 EOL claim (the only source cited was actually GHES 3.17's docs page, not 3.18's — not a real source for this date — compounded by the known id.ts fuzzy-dedupe collision risk with the existing 3.17 entry), and an EU AI Act CSAM/NCII-generation ban (law-firm-blog sourcing only, and title overlaps enough with two existing Dec 2 EU AI Act entries to risk a bad fuzzy-merge).
concerns: Google Cloud Next 2027 (Apr 13-15, Mandalay Bay) is now unconfirmed via a primary source (cloud.google.com/blog.google) for a 6th consecutive run — every source is a third-party event-aggregator. A maintainer with different fetch access should settle this directly; the entry is left as previously filed rather than touched again on the same weak sourcing.

Likely a third instance of this project's standing dedupe-threshold issue; not fixable from this run (no hand-editing data/, no editing src/).

A third such pair: data/events/2027-02.json has 'OpenAI retires whisper-1 and gpt-4o-transcribe family' and 'OpenAI retires Whisper-1 and GPT-4o transcription models', both dated 2027-02-26, same org, near-identical fact. Flagging alongside the other two for whoever eventually revisits src/lib/id.ts's token-overlap threshold — three independent collisions now on record across three different runs' worth of filings.

The Azure OpenAI GPT-4o retirement date remains unresolved: the existing calendar entry says Dec 9 2026, but a devtools/cloud lane search again surfaced a conflicting Oct 1 2026 retirement claim (this time via privatedevops.com, a low-quality aggregator quoting Microsoft Foundry docs, not learn.microsoft.com itself). Left untouched again rather than risk overwriting a possibly-correct entry with a possibly-wrong one; flagged in at least two prior runs' logs too.

EU AI Act coverage for Dec 2, 2026 may already be double-filed: data/events/2026-12.json has both 'EU AI Act synthetic-content labeling duty takes effect' and 'EU AI Act watermarking grace period ends for already-deployed systems', which read like the same Article 50 obligation described twice.
